Implementation Details
In this chapter we describe the approach used to store the normalized unit group of the group algebra in the library, and to reconstruct the group V(KG) from the stored information.
Saving the data
To compute the pc-presentation of the normalized unit group of the modular group algebra of a finite p-group we used the function PcNormalizedUnitGroup from the &LAGUNA; package. It uses the algorithm descibed in . See the &LAGUNA; manual for more details.
When this group is computed, we store its pc presentation. For the polycyclic generating sequence g_1, \ldots, g_l of V(KG) these are the power relations g_i^p, 1 \leq i \leq l, and the commutator relations [g_j, g_i], 1 \leq i < j \leq l, in this order. Each right-hand side is a word g_{k_1}^{e_1} \cdots g_{k_m}^{e_m}, and most of them are short.
The file unitlib/data/u<n>.g holds the groups of order n, one line per group: [ id, ref, relations, exponents, dimensionBasis, weights ]. If ref is 0, the string relations lists the nontrivial relations. Groups with consecutive catalogue numbers tend to have similar presentations, so otherwise it lists only the relations that differ from those of the group ref, which precedes id in the same block of 32 groups. The entries are separated by spaces. Each consists of the number of the relation, the character ! if the entry replaces the relation (otherwise its exponents are added to those of the relation modulo p), and the generators k_1, \ldots, k_m. Relation numbers and generators are written as differences to their predecessor, and the exponents e_1, \ldots, e_m of all entries follow in the string exponents, which is empty for p = 2. Every number is written in base 26, most significant digit first, with the digits a to z, except for the last digit, which is A to Z.
For a group G of prime order p no data is stored: V(KG) is elementary abelian of order p^{(p-1)}, since KG \cong K[y]/(y^p) with y = g - 1 and (1 + y^i)^p = 1 + y^{ip} = 1.
The data files are plain text in the source repository and are compressed with gzip when the package is released; &GAP; reads either form.
There is one more thing that needs to be stored together with this code to make it sure that we will correctly identify the underlying group G of the group algebra KG with its image in the pc-presentation of the normalized unit group V(KG).
The group G is extracted from the &GAP; Small Groups Library, so it is always the same, unless its description in the library will be changed (and it will be an important task of &UnitLib; maintaner to update the package in this case!), and here we are safe from inconsistencies.
But the next stage is the computation of generators of the normalized unit group V(KG), and the first step is the dimension basis of the group G, that can be computed using the &LAGUNA; function DimensionBasis. To avoid the influence of possible changes in &GAP; or usage of random methods, we store (in compacted form) the information about the dimension basis of G in the &UnitLib;.
All further procedures are implemented inside the &LAGUNA; package, and their result is uniquely determined and predictable.
For the reader interested in more details, the package contains the file unitlib/lib/genlib.g with the function CreatePcNormalizedUnitGroupsLibrary, that saves the descriptions for groups of a given prime power order, and the function CreatePcNormalizedUnitGroupsLibraryFile, that combines them into a library file.
Reading the data
To reconstruct the normalized unit group V(KG) from the library, we need only to know the catalogue number of the underlying group G in the &GAP; Small Groups Library.
We use the same numbering as in the &GAP; Small Group Library, so &UnitLib; finds the appropriate library file and reads from it the relations of the pc presentation of V(KG) and the information about the dimension basis of G used for their computation.
Then &UnitLib; decodes the relations, applying the differences along the chain of references, and creates V(KG) as a pc group with a single collector (see ). It skips the consistency check, since the stored presentation is consistent. We also create G using the &GAP; Small Groups Library.
Now to glue the group V(KG) with the underlying group G properly, the value of the attribute of G is set in accordance with the data retrieved from the library. This will guarantee the correct construction of
and by the &LAGUNA; package.
It remains now to make only several technical steps, such as constructing the group algebra KG over the appropriate field K, and storing KG in the attribute of V(KG) and V(KG) in the attribute of KG.
